title: Grateful Dead Live at Seattle Center Arena on 1971-01-24

ai_review.summary: A high‑energy Seattle 1/24/71 show packed with Pigpen’s Lovelight magic, captured on a decent soundboard tape.
ai_review.review: The recording preserves an incendiary late‑night performance highlighted by multiple Lovelights, a scorching Hard to Handle and a standout Sunshine Daydream. Reviewers rave about the powerful Pigpen organ and vocals, strong Garcia leads, and tight rhythm section, while noting occasional vocal saturation and a bit of tape flutter. Overall the show is described as hot, seamless and unforgettable.

ai_rating.rationale: 27 reviews overwhelmingly give 4‑5 stars, praising both performance and sound quality; a few low‑star comments note tape quirks but do not outweigh the positive consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear soundboard capture (crisp Sunshine Daydream, clean organ), though some listeners mention occasional distortion/over‑saturated vocals, slight flutter and mono mix quirks.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Mixed‑up setlist with multiple Lovelights and seamless transitions; the band kept the energy high even after a curfew break, extending into early morning.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead work shines early (Cumberland Blues solo, strong tone) and drives the show, though some later sections are noted as sloppy.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is powerful (“Phil bombs”) and anchors the jams, especially during transitions into Uncle John’s Band.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir provides solid rhythm guitar and vocal harmonies; early vocals were a bit high but overall strong.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann delivers stellar foot‑pedal work and a standout solo; Mickey Hart adds his signature cowbell and the duo’s drum duet is highlighted as a rare, energetic moment.
